instructions:
Note text view v1. This is an authoring view of the original named note at its existing source:// address, not a Markdown file. Do not add .md or replace names with IDs. Use CommonMark headings, paragraphs, lists, task lists, fenced code, quotes, dividers and LaTeX formulas: \(...\) for inline math and \[...\] for display math (put display delimiters on separate lines in their own paragraph, with blank lines before and after). Use these delimiters when writing notes; do not wrap formulas in code or use $ or $$ as the authoring convention. Dollar-based editor shortcuts are separate UI actions. Ordinary [label](URL) links are distinct from object references. Internal links use source:// addresses, including in note content. Reference kind is a separate XML attribute; use the corresponding library/notes/writings/agents/assets namespace. Internal resource URIs exclusively use source://; no alternate protocol is supported. XML extensions are strict and case-sensitive. Unknown tags/attributes and arbitrary HTML are rejected. XML uses standard entity escaping; use CDATA when text contains raw Markdown with < or &. Code and math treat XML literally. Inline: label Markdown, inline Markdown, inline Markdown. , , and wrap inline Markdown with explicit bold, italic, or strike styling when delimiter boundaries would be ambiguous. Preserve numeric character references such as at text boundaries; they represent literal whitespace, not formatting. Colors: default,gray,brown,orange,yellow,green,blue,purple,pink,red. Blocks: , . Import an attachment or captured image only from a discovered authorized attachmentId or captureId using src="import://handle". The backend copies its verified bytes into managed staging and returns an asset handle in subsequent reads. A normal hyperlink never imports bytes. preserves object-reference snapshots. represents a child page, not an ordinary link. Removing it proposes recycling that child's subtree. Add File uses an authorized parent note source:// address and title frontmatter to create a child; the backend returns its allocated address. Move to uses source://notes/parent-id as the new parent, or source://notes/ to move to root, preserving the moved page ID. Normal reads and returned addresses always use source://notes/page-id.
preserves ragged or empty tables. GFM tables are allowed for rectangular tables; separator lines are syntax, not extra note rows. represents a collapsible list item. Put its child blocks in immediately afterward; children remain readable/editable while the UI is collapsed. A heading followed by is a toggle heading; toggle="false" or removing that attribute makes it a regular heading. Open/closed is local reading state, not document content. Do not use > for toggles: CommonMark > remains a quote. immediately follows its parent block. immediately follows the block it formats. Unknown future blocks are represented by an opaque ; preserve or move it unchanged, or remove it explicitly. Never invent opaque or asset handles. The frontmatter is exactly --- / title: a YAML string / ---. Do not add document IDs, block IDs, versions or internal JSON. Patch expected lines must match exactly and uniquely. Add distinguishing context on ambiguity. Read before updating/deleting. New note changes are saved together with a separate review baseline; pending Diff remains until user Keep/Undo. Saving does not mean Keep. Historical results marked proposed are not saved; recover their original request instead of replaying. Reads default to current content; view=saved selects acknowledged saved content.

examples.title: Replace one uniquely matched paragraph
examples.patch:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: source://notes/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001
@@
-Original paragraph.
+Revised paragraph.
*** End Patch
